target_customer: Banks, credit unions and fintechs that need to connect core banking systems and third party products
problem: Financial institutions struggle to integrate legacy core systems with fintech products and each other. Sandbox sold a low-code integration platform called Glyue.
business_model: B2B software licenses and subscriptions to financial institutions

founders.name: Ravi Balasubramanian
founders.background_notes: A search result described his profile as mentioning Harvard endowment investing; the page was not opened, so it is not recorded as employment.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building adapters for many core banking and fintech APIs with batch and event driven jobs is standard integration engineering with domain knowledge of banking cores.

defensibility.rationale: Once banks build integrations in the platform they are costly to move, but low-code integration tools were widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying it; nCino acquired the company in February 2025.

market_need_then: Banks and credit unions relied on aging cores that were hard to connect to fintech products; a later Forbes piece cited by press release called this a zombie core crisis.

rebrands.why: Product renamed after the nCino acquisition; nCino's page notes it as formerly Glyue.

brand_strength.rationale: Glyue, pronounced glue, is a memorable product name, but sources show no mascot or community and the company sold to a narrow B2B audience.

outcome_analysis: Sandbox Banking sold its Glyue integration platform to banks and credit unions for years on very little outside capital, raising a $4.3M seed in February 2023 that brought total financing to about $6M. nCino acquired it in February 2025, reported at about $52.5M. This is a capital efficient niche B2B outcome with a modest exit.
notes: Founded year left null: an aggregator says 2014 and says the company was formerly AlphaPack; not verified. The $52.5M price comes from financedirectoreurope; another source says $52.5M to $62.5M. An aggregator lists $5.8M in November 2022, conflicting with the February 2023 $4.3M announcement, so only the press-release round is recorded. Earlier funding before 2023 (about $1.7M implied by the $6M total) is unaccounted for. Competitor search returned only current aggregator comparison pages, so the list is empty. Founder backgrounds not found.
